device.name: BrickSim state-based Lego assemble-brick environment (Isaac Lab)

facts.text: The assemble-brick package registers Lego-AssembleBrick-v0 with entry point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv and env_cfg_entry_point <this package>.env:AssembleBrickEnvCfg
The same package registers Lego-AssembleBrick-RGB-v0 and Lego-AssembleBrick-RGBD-v0 with the RGB and RGB-D configuration classes
The Python package requires Python 3.11 or newer and depends on gymnasium 1.2.0
The isaacsim and isaaclab optional extras pin isaacsim[all,extscache]==5.1.0 and isaaclab==2.3.2.post1
BrickSim requires an x86-64 Linux platform and an NVIDIA driver compatible with Isaac Sim
The scene runs one environment instance with an environment spacing of 5.0
Each control step applies 6 simulation steps of 1/60 s and an episode is 12.0 s long
AssembleBrickEnvCfg removes the hand, front and side cameras and the image observation group, so the state-based environment returns no images
The arm action is a differential inverse-kinematics relative pose command
The arm action is scaled per axis by (0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
The gripper action opens the fingers to 0.04 m above the 0.2 threshold and closes them to 0.0 m below the -0.2 threshold
The ActionsCfg docstring tells callers to send finite actions in [-1, 1]
The policy observation group is end-effector pose, gripper width, gripper speed, brick pose and target pose
The privileged observation group adds brick_grasped, connection_created and brick_dimensions and sets concatenate_terms to False
The termination terms are a timeout, a formed target connection with the gripper open, a non-target connection and a brick dropped below its height threshold
A reset applies a Gaussian joint offset with mean 0.0 and standard deviation 0.02
A reset places the brick uniformly over x 0.36 to 0.56 m, y 0.16 to 0.32 m and yaw 0 to 2*pi

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial brick gap; the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions.  The fake draws with Python's random.Random; upstream Isaac Lab seeds its own torch/numpy generators through the manager-based environment, and the two were never compared

gaps: rigid-body physics, contacts, friction, actuators and sensors are Isaac Sim's, configured by this package but implemented outside it (python/pyproject.toml:17-19); the gate cannot import, install or run Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab, so nothing here was executed against them
the state-based configuration is served; the RGB and RGB-D camera variants return 720x1280 RGB and depth images, which this driver does not declare, and no image array is produced
the fake backend is a pure Python kinematic stand-in, not Isaac Sim: it has no contact, friction, actuator, sensor or camera model, and its reward is a placeholder, not the weights of env.py:446-455

the fake keeps a scalar gap to the brick instead of the full articulation; its observation keeps the structure of the policy and privileged groups but the policy group is 23 numbers and the RGB/RGB-D image groups of the other configurations are absent
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
